title: "Section 2.1: Introduction to Quarto Docs"
---

### 1. Opening A New Quarto Document

To open a new Quarto document, click the **New** icon on the top left corner of Position and select **New File...**. This will prompt another dropdown menu in the top center of Positron. Select **Quarto Document**.

![](/figs/sec_0201_gif_1.gif)

::: {.callout-warning}
If you opened a new Quarto document but do not see the template, then you may need to hide the lower panel. You can do this by {{< kbd Ctrl >}} + {{< kbd j >}} in Windows or {{< kbd command >}} + {{< kbd j >}} in macOS.
:::

### 2. The YAML Header

Any new Quarto document includes a document header called YAML header. YAML lets us set options to how we want the document to look. The YAML header is enclosed by two sets of `---` (lines 1 and 4) and it is within this set of `---` we will specify our YAML mappings.

``` {.yaml filename="Untitled-1.qmd"}
---
title: "Untitled"
format: html
---
```

Rewrite your YAML header so it looks like

``` {.yaml filename='Untitled-1.qmd'}
---
title: "CIS 351: Week X Lecture Y"
subtitle: "Today's Topic"
author: "Your Name"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
---
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## YAML Syntax

1. Be sure that your code looks exactly like mine. Except for the text inside quotation marks, you must follow the same punctuation and capitalization as shown above.
2. There is one indent in front of `html:` on line 6 and two indents in front of `embed-resources: true` on line 7.
:::

Although this is optional, but it is a good idea to check the **Render on Save** box so Positron will automatically save the file for you whenever it renders the Quarto document.

![](/figs/sec_0201_fig_1.png){width=50% fig-align="center"}

### 3. Saving the Quarto Document

To save the current Quarto document, go to the top menu bar and click on **File**, then select **Save As...**. A new window will open where you can to navigate to the appropriate folder (`Week X`, `Homework`, etc). If the Quarto document is lecture notes, then use the file name `week_x_lecture_y.qmd`. If it is a homework assignment, then use the file name `assignment_x_last_name.qmd`.

::: convention
1. If you are using a Mac, make sure that your file name ends with `.qmd`.
2. Only use lowercase letters in file names, and always use `_` as the word separator. For example, `week_x_lecture_y.qmd`, _not_ `Week x lecture y.qmd`
:::

### 4. Writing Content in the Quarto Document

For the most part, content in a Quarto document are written in **Quarto markdown** (which is why Quarto documents use the `.qmd` file extension). Quarto markdown is a derivative of the **markdown** language.
